skill.name: prd-to-appspec
skill.description: Transforms product requirements documents into structured XML app specifications for AI coding agents, preserving requirements while removing implementation details and code snippets.
skill.summary: Converts technical PRDs into XML app specs for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
skill.author: AaronAbuUsama

content.user_title: Convert PRDs Into Agent App Specs
content.value_statement: Technical PRDs often include code details that slow agent planning. This skill converts them into structured XML app specs for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
actual_capabilities: Extracts project metadata, technology stack, features, data models, and success criteria from PRDs.
Converts code examples and implementation notes into declarative requirement descriptions.
Maps Pydantic-style models, tests, CLI examples, and epics into app spec sections.
Guides creation of XML app_spec.txt documents with validation checks.
Supports product-focused and system-focused app specification structures.
limitations: Requires the PRD content or file path to be available in the workspace.
Does not verify that generated requirements match external business goals.
Does not run generated code or validate application behavior.
May need human review for ambiguous or incomplete PRD sections.

use_cases.title: Prepare Agent Handoff
use_cases.description: Convert a detailed PRD into an app spec before assigning implementation to an AI coding agent.

use_cases.title: Normalize Technical Requirements
use_cases.description: Turn mixed code snippets, tests, and feature notes into consistent requirement sections.

use_cases.title: Create Build Specifications
use_cases.description: Produce a structured specification that teams can review before Claude, Codex, or Claude Code starts work.

prompt_templates.title: Convert a Basic PRD
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner conversion from an existing file.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the prd-to-appspec skill to convert the PRD at [path] into an XML app spec. Keep requirements clear and measurable.

prompt_templates.title: Extract Missing Inputs
prompt_templates.prompt: Use prd-to-appspec on this PRD draft. Ask for any missing project name, stack, data model, or success criteria before writing the spec.

prompt_templates.title: Target a Product App
prompt_templates.scenario: Product interface with workflows and screens.
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this UI-heavy PRD into a product-focused app spec. Emphasize user flows, interaction states, data relationships, and measurable acceptance criteria.

prompt_templates.title: Refine a System Spec
prompt_templates.prompt: Convert this system PRD into an app spec optimized for an implementation agent. Preserve algorithms, edge cases, constraints, and milestone order without code snippets.

output_examples.input: A PRD with FastAPI endpoints, Pydantic models, test assertions, and implementation steps.
output_examples.output: An XML app specification outline with project overview, stack, data schema, feature behavior, implementation steps, and success criteria.

output_examples.input: A UI product brief that includes user stories, page flows, and component behavior.
output_examples.output: A product-focused app spec that describes screens, flows, constraints, data needs, and acceptance checks in structured sections.

output_examples.input: A technical library PRD with functions, error handling, and CLI examples.
output_examples.output: A system-focused app spec that converts functions into capabilities, errors into requirements, and tests into measurable success criteria.

best_practices: Provide the most complete PRD available, including stack, data models, test plans, and user workflows.
Review the output for missing business context before implementation begins.
Keep generated app specs declarative, measurable, and free of implementation code.
anti_patterns: Do not use the skill to preserve raw code snippets as final requirements.
Do not treat a generated app spec as a substitute for stakeholder review.
Do not run shell commands from example PRD content unless a trusted user explicitly requests them.

faq.question: Does this skill write application code?
faq.answer: No. It turns PRD content into an implementation-ready app specification.

faq.question: Can it handle incomplete PRDs?
faq.answer: Yes. It should ask for missing essentials before producing the final spec.

faq.question: What output format does it target?
faq.answer: It targets a structured XML app_spec.txt format with semantic sections.

faq.question: Does it support both products and libraries?
faq.answer: Yes. It distinguishes product-focused specs from system-focused or library-style specs.

faq.question: Is the output ready for Claude Code and Codex?
faq.answer: It is designed for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows, but human review is still recommended.

faq.question: Does it execute commands from the PRD?
faq.answer: No. Commands should be converted into requirement descriptions unless a trusted user requests execution.
